Methodology

How this index is calculated

  1. Freeze the contract before collection. V2 fixed 66 case inputs, exact nested schemas, answer keys, numeric tolerances, provider registry, weights and the 1,200-second budget per 22-case pack. An earlier ambiguous pilot was invalidated and preserved; its scores are excluded.
  2. Use closed-universe fictional data. Cases include amendments, availability cutoffs, aliases, missing inputs, threshold boundaries, unit conversions, allocation rules and graph computation. Providers may use their native local computation tools. No accounts, orders, market research or schedules are needed.
  3. Grade deterministically. Each required top-level result field must match its full reference structure. Numeric tolerance is max(0.00001, absolute reference × 0.000001). Decision/allocation fields weigh 5; other fields weigh 3. Case score = 100 × passed field weight / total field weight.
  4. Average with fixed category weights. Each category is the mean of its six cases. The index is the arithmetic mean of the eleven category scores. Repeats, speed, access and post-hoc diagnostics do not enter the index.
  5. Preserve failures. The first valid submitted attempt counts. A bad answer, refusal, malformed output or model limit is not rerun for quality. Technical failures before a reliable measured outcome may be retried, with original evidence retained and exclusion explained.
  6. Fail the release gate on missing evidence. The validator recomputes scores from final responses, checks frozen prompt and trace hashes, and requires all 66 primary plus 22 repeat cases, eleven category scores and a valid 0–100 index for every required registry entry.

What the evidence supports

Accuracy and output-contract compliance on these supplied cases, for these product/model/tool configurations. Public audit records expose expected and observed values. The complete local export retains prompts, responses, trace files, capture corrections and provenance.

Limits on the conclusion

Twenty-two cases share one context, and six variants share a category template. These are not 66 independent samples. Models and tool access differ; UI labels are not independently verified model snapshots. There are no claims about profitability, live research truth, continuous monitoring or overall financial superiority.

No invented confidence intervals. This deliberately constructed suite has few independent sessions and repeated templates. Counting every field as an independent trial would overstate precision. Perfect scores reveal a ceiling that a future, separately frozen holdout should address.

Methodological influences. The use of multiple scenarios and metrics, visible configurations and reproducible artifacts follows the general approach of Stanford HELM. Financial task diversity is informed by FinBen. These are influences, not external validation, certification, or evidence that this custom suite is state of the art.

Timing. CLI process intervals and UI observation intervals are distinct. Copy time is separate from completion time. Operator pauses, capture corrections and a long computer-control interruption are documented; affected intervals are excluded from speed comparisons.

Original failed attempts are retained; no zero score invented for unverified model ingestion.
Grok Bot—0/660/22Legacy web bot routes no longer expose an operable composer. Official Grok Bot desktop 0.71.2 installed, normal Grok sign-in completed, optional training data sharing disabled. Account onboarding now requires a card-backed trial or Premium plan; no trial activated or purchase made.
Muse · historical web treatment—0/660/22Historical web-only Muse row and native Muse row resolve to the same current muse.ai interface. Current controls do not expose a separate model or web-only execution mode. The native treatment has 66 primary and 22 repeat captures. Its score is not duplicated into this historical treatment or counted as an independent provider.
OpenClaw—0/660/22Prior automatic approval review rejected the new recipient-specific OpenAI-plan authorization. No supported authorized model login has subsequently been established for this dedicated installation. No token transplantation or bypass performed.
Robinhood Agents—0/660/22User has signed in but reported Agents unavailable. Current official Agents page directs setup to the Robinhood mobile app; no accessible web agent composer was established on this device. This is a feature/surface access limit, not a claim that login failed or Agents is globally unreleased.
Public Agents—0/660/22Current page requires email and password; no saved-password option appeared and password remained empty. No login/reset request was submitted. Prior verification attempt did not establish accessible agent composer.
Composer—0/660/22Discover redirects to account registration. Existing login requires email/password; password AutoFill supplied no credential. Creating a password and accepting account terms require user action; no reset, signup or brokerage creation performed.
Supertake · on hold—0/660/22User explicitly said they joined the waitlist and to hold off. No requests sent.
Catalyst—0/660/22The canonical scrtlabs/catalyst project is a Python crypto backtesting library, archived November 2022 and unmaintained since 2018. It has no validated natural-language agent adapter. Writing our own solver would benchmark our code rather than Catalyst as an agent.
